description: A sub-word piece the model reads and writes. Roughly four characters of English; code, numbers and other languages use more tokens for the same content.
The maximum tokens one call can hold, input and output together: the model's entire working memory for that call.
Reshapes the next-token distribution: low is focused and repetitive, high is varied and riskier. Zero approximates always picking the most likely token.
Nucleus sampling: sample only from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to p.
Identical requests can return different outputs even at temperature 0, because of batching, floating-point order, expert routing and serving updates.
Fluent, confident output that is false or unsupported, including invented citations.
The date the training data ends. Later facts must come from the context (retrieval, tools).
The tendency to agree with the user or abandon a correct answer under pushback.
Uneven use of the context: the middle of long inputs is used less, and judges tend to favor the first option shown.
